/itineraryStops/4/description.source_en:
**The ⟦G0⟧ in Korea (재한유엔기념공원, UNMCK)** is the **only United Nations memorial cemetery anywhere in the world** — established January 18, 1951 by the UN Command during the Korean War, dedicated April 6, 1951 by US General Matthew Ridgway, and formally donated to the United Nations by the Republic of Korea in **1959** in gratitude for the UN forces who died defending South Korea. 

**22 sending nations participated in the Korean War (1950-1953)** under the UN flag — 16 nations sent combat troops + 5 sent medical aid + 1 sent observers. Initially up to **11,000 graves** were here; most fallen were repatriated post-armistice, leaving today **2,300 graves from 11 countries** (UK, US, Türkiye, Canada, Australia, Netherlands, France, Norway, South Korea, New Zealand, South Africa). 

The visit walks the cemetery's main monumental sequence: (1) the **Main Gate** (designed by Korean architect Kim Joong-up, built by Busan City in 1966 — the eight roof-supporting pillars symbolize the moment and eternity of soldiers' standing watch); (2) the **Memorial Service Hall** featuring a 12-minute documentary in English/Korean on the cemetery's history; (3) the **Symbolic Area** where the **22 sending-state flags + Korean + UN flag** fly daily; (4) the **Wall of Remembrance**, completed **2006**, with all **40,896 UN casualty names inscribed on 140 marble panels** — many veterans' relatives find their ancestors here for the first time; and (5) the **US Korean War Memorial**, dedicated **2013** with the Frank Gaylord sculpture commissioned by the American Battle Monuments Commission. 

**Hours: 09:00-18:00 (May-Sep) / 09:00-17:00 (Oct-Apr); FREE; 100% wheelchair-accessible**. Annual **'Turn Toward Busan' silent ceremony** Nov 11 11:00 AM, where the world turns symbolically toward this cemetery.

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/1.source_en: Origins: **1920s-1930s** Busan administration relocation + **1955 Taegeukdo refugees** (~800 families)

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/5.source_en: **~1.4 million visitors annually** since the public-art revitalization

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/6.source_en: **Living residential community** — quiet voices, no drones, no flash into homes

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/7.source_en: Free village entry; optional Stamp Map ~₩2,000

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/8.source_en: **UN-HABITAT Asian Townscape Award 2012** — recognition of the 2009 'Dreaming of Machu Picchu' art project that transformed the 1955 Taegeukdo refugee settlement into Busan's signature mural village

/itineraryStops/5/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Residents live here — keep voices down, no drones, take rubbish with you; wear grippy shoes for the steep lanes; afternoon golden hour ~16:00-17:00 is the village's best light

/itineraryStops/5/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Hanbok rental, craft workshops, Korean candy stalls, cafes; small village museum at the entrance; the stamp map is the easiest way to navigate

/itineraryStops/5/whyOnRoute.source_en: The route's **most colorful and unique** stop — there is no other neighborhood like this anywhere in Korea. The Korean War refugee narrative directly threads from ⟦G0⟧ (the moral memorial) → Gamcheon (the lived consequence: refugee settlement that became a community) → Jagalchi (the economic consequence: ajumma fish-vendors supporting their families). The 15:30 arrival lands ahead of the 18:00 info-center close while still giving guests ~1 hour of golden-hour light over the rainbow rooftops, the village's most photogenic time.

/itineraryStops/5/convenience/restroom.source_en: Public restrooms at the Tourist Information Center and around the main viewpoints
